question: At the exact observed population counts, which reaction rates would change if occupations were spatially random?
basis: Added after the independent-site homogeneous modes were found stable. This is a permutation expectation on ledger snapshots only. It introduces no alternative physical evolution.
inputs: All archived trajectories in the old and new measurements. All their recorded time windows.
method: Condition on the reacting material state. When the reaction uses a neighboring fuel or waste site, condition on that site too. Under a uniform permutation at fixed I, B, F, and W counts, the remaining B-neighbor count is hypergeometric. Compute the exact finite-volume expectation of the local rate, then time-average over the ledger. Compare with the realized accepted count per time over the same window, separately for all four directions and for total net B.
restriction: The random-placement expectation is instantaneous. The counterfactual does not retain observed bonds or imply the mixed world would stay at the imposed state fractions.
